text:
Detroit's captaincy is vacant and its best-known player is somewhere between Detroit and a trade. Dylan Larkin asked out, refused to play until he's moved, and was suspended by the club at the end of October; this week's headlines have Minnesota reportedly presenting the best offer and Montreal reportedly willing to meet the asking price. Until something happens, the Red Wings play on without him, and lately it shows. They're winless in four, outscored 13-5, with 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that stretch. Their playoff chance on our numbers has slipped to about 19%.

The goaltending hasn't bailed them out. John Gibson is at .856 over his last five starts, 4.2 goals worse than the shots deserved, and .866 on the season. The frustrating part for Todd McLellan is that some of the scoring chances are there: Viktor Arvidsson has 3.3 expected goals in four pointless games and no goals in six. We have him at 33% to score tonight, level with Alex DeBrincat.

Florida is missing its own spine. Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are both on injured reserve with knee injuries, though the headlines this week say both are getting close. In the meantime Matthew Tkachuk has seven assists in a five-game point streak and has eight points in his last four games against Detroit, and Sam Reinhart is two points from 700. Sandis Vilmanis returns, and Akira Schmid starts in goal, per The Hockey News.

The two teams met ten days ago and Detroit won 5-3, which feels like a long time ago now. Watch the penalty box: Florida takes 5.7 penalties a game and draws 5.8, and its power play is the strongest unit in this game at 1.17 expected goals a night. Our numbers lean Florida slightly on chances, 3.25 expected goals to 2.94.
headline: Detroit plays on around the Larkin standoff
